narration: We start with the input scene view. A camera ray is cast from the viewpoint and a sample point p is picked along it inside the room.
The point p is looked up in a multi-resolution feature grid: coarse and fine voxel grids each give an interpolated feature at that location.
The concatenated multi-resolution features are passed through a small MLP decoder.
The decoder outputs a vector of signed distance values, one per object in the scene, so every object gets its own SDF at this point.
Taking the minimum across all per-object SDFs gives the scene SDF, the distance to the nearest surface of any object.
Each per-object SDF is converted into an object density profile along the ray.
Multiplying object density by scene transmittance yields the occlusion-aware object opacity, which is supervised against the instance masks by the opacity loss.
The scene SDF also drives scene transmittance, which combined with scene density forms the volume rendering weight function along the ray.
Those weights render depth, normal and colour images. Depth and normal losses use pretrained-model cues, and the reconstruction loss compares the rendered image with the input view.
Finally, two regularisers act on the SDF vector: an Eikonal loss on the gradient norm, and a ReLU regulariser keeping the scene SDF consistent with the per-object SDFs.
